messages.author: a27a46fa1c1d735a
messages.subject: thickness of geom_point symbols
parts:
Hello everybody,

I made a scatter plot using unfilled circles (shape=1) where each
circle
represents a scoreline (home goals & away goals). The problem I'm
having
now is that when I save the plot as PostScript (or PDF) [1] the
circles are
drawn too thick and some regions of the plot come out as black blobs,
whereas on screen[2] it can be clearly seen that the regions in
question have
a different density of circles.
So, is there any way to adjust the thickness of the symbols in a
scatter plot?
I already tried increasing the size of the plot but it's no use and it
has to fit
into an A4 paper anyway.

[1] http://i1084.photobucket.com/albums/j419/lottinray/screenshots/postscript_output.png
[2] http://i1084.photobucket.com/albums/j419/lottinray/screenshots/screen_output.png

Thanks in advance!
Ernest

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: thickness of geom_point symbols
parts:
Hi:

It would seem to me that when plotting discrete data like this,
geom_tile() would be a more compact way of displaying it. Here's a
reproducible example:

goals <- data.frame(home = sample(0:4, 10000, replace = TRUE,
prob = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.1, 0.06, 0.04)),
away = sample(0:4, 10000, replace = TRUE,
prob = c(0.55, 0.3, 0.09, 0.05, 0.01)))
with(goals, table(home, away))

# Convert table to data frame for use in ggplot2
goalDF <- as.data.frame(with(goals, table(home, away)))

# Convert factors to numeric
goalDF <- within(goalDF, {
home = as.numeric(as.character(home))
away = as.numeric(as.character(away)) } )
str(goalDF)

# Plot:
library('ggplot2')
ggplot(goalDF, aes(x = away, y = home, fill = Freq)) +
theme_bw() +
geom_tile() +
scale_y_reverse() +
labs(x = 'Away goals', y = 'Home goals') +
geom_text(aes(label = paste(Freq/100, '%', sep = ''))) +
scale_fill_gradientn(colours = topo.colors(12), legend = FALSE)

If you prefer the actual numbers rather than percentages, then use
label = Freq within geom_text() instead. There are also several
different color palettes one could use instead of topo.colors.

HTH,
Dennis

>> with(goals, table(home, away))
>>
>> # Convert table to data frame for use in ggplot2
>> goalDF <- as.data.frame(with(goals, table(home, away)))
>>
>> # Convert factors to numeric
>> goalDF <- within(goalDF, {
>>           home = as.numeric(as.character(home))
>>           away = as.numeric(as.character(away))    } )
>> str(goalDF)
>>
>> # Plot:
>> library('ggplot2')
>> ggplot(goalDF, aes(x = away, y = home, fill = Freq)) +
>>      theme_bw() +
>>      geom_tile() +
>>      scale_y_reverse() +
>>      labs(x = 'Away goals', y = 'Home goals') +
>>      geom_text(aes(label = paste(Freq/100, '%', sep = ''))) +
